$comment: Gate B DRAFT rule object for RF-FIELD-001 — pending, NON-EXECUTABLE. Authored only from RF Clinical Rule Specification v1.2 §13.2 and the RF-FIELD-001 inventory entry. Clinical-content-only rule: cites an evidence claim and has NO architecture references (architecture_refs intentionally empty per v1.2 §4.3). Expresses Aspetar speed-milestone REFERENCE structure only: at least 70%, 80%, and 95% of maximum sprint speed appear as Aspetar phase-exit criteria for Accumulation, Transition, and Simulation. These are pathway-specific expert criteria usable ONLY when the maximum-sprint-speed denominator is valid and the context is sufficiently similar; they are NOT universal mandatory thresholds, NOT proof of readiness, and must not be used with an unknown or unreliable denominator. No dosage, sprint/speed progression, exercise selection, field plan, complete rehab plan, RTT, or RTS logic; tolerance of one field domain does not clear another; safety precedence preserved; does not bypass RF-RECUR-001/002, RF-REHAB-001..006, RF-SEV-005, RF-DX-006, or RF-SAF-006. Not approved. Not wired into any runtime.

input_contract.$comment: The reference milestones and pathway context taken verbatim from v1.2 §13.2. Usable only when the MSS denominator is valid and the context is sufficiently similar; raw media is never interpreted here.

decision_contract.$comment: Speed-milestone reference structure only. Milestones are pathway-specific reference criteria, valid only with a valid MSS denominator and sufficiently similar context; they are not universal thresholds, not readiness proof, and clear no field domain. No dosage, progression schedule, exercise selection, field/rehab plan, RTT, or RTS. Safety precedence preserved.

notes: Clinical_content normative source; MAY; permitted_use logic_with_uncertainty. Architecture references are intentionally empty: per v1.2 §4.3 clinical-content rules cite valid evidence_claim_ids and do not carry architecture refs (none in §13.2); [] means 'none in source', not 'missing'. Evidence grade/role preserved per source: QRF-024 (E1) is conditional pathway-milestone reference evidence only. Reference milestones preserved exactly from §13.2: at least 70%, 80%, and 95% of maximum sprint speed appear as Aspetar phase-exit criteria for Accumulation, Transition, and Simulation respectively. Permitted use preserved exactly: pathway-specific expert criteria only when the athlete's maximum sprint speed denominator is valid and the context is sufficiently similar; denominator-quality and population/context limits are required. Prohibited use preserved exactly: not universal mandatory thresholds, not proof of readiness, and not usable with an unknown or unreliable (or self-estimated-without-validation / stale / context-mismatched) denominator. Tolerance of running or sprinting does not automatically clear kicking, and tolerance of one field domain does not clear another (consistent with RF-RECUR-002 and §13.1). The rule creates no speed/sprint progression schedule, dosage, work-to-rest ratios, exercise selection, complete field plan, complete rehab plan, RTT, or RTS, and speed-milestone achievement alone is neither progression authority nor readiness. Safety-state choice (read §13.2 exactly): §13.2 does NOT assign a closed V3.1 safety state, so safety_state_output is null and blocked_targets is empty, and the speed-milestone limits are represented in decision_contract; no safety state was inferred by analogy. It does not bypass RF-RECUR-001/002, RF-REHAB-001..006, RF-SEV-005, RF-DX-006, or RF-SAF-006, and does not override RF-SAF-006, RF-DX-006, RF-DX-008, RF-SEV-004, RF-SEV-005, RF-RECUR-001, or RF-RECUR-002; uncertainty is preserved when MSS denominator quality, measurement method, population similarity, phase context, field-exposure, capacity, schedule, monitoring, or sport-demand evidence is incomplete. Running/sprinting reference rule, not a safety rule. No field-exposure engine is authored here (deferred to the later field, rehab, and readiness objects). Draft — approval_status remains pending.
